name: pbv-mw-ext-bitwise
help: in the pbv-mw pass, pull an extension out of bitwise operators: `OP(EXT n a, EXT n b) -> EXT n (OP a b)` for OP in pbvand/pbvor/pbvxor and both extensions of the same kind over equal-width sources, and `pbvnot (psign_extend n a) -> psign_extend n (pbvnot a)`. Extensions of the same kind over sources of different widths are aligned first, `EXT (t-a) x -> EXT (t-b) (EXT (b-a) x)` when a <= b is entailed. Also strips a common extension from an equality, `(= (EXT n a) (EXT n b)) -> (= a b)`, which is sound since both extensions are injective, and folds `a OP (pbvnot a)` to its constant. Implies the pbv-mw pass is run. Disabled by default. NOTE: the conditional rules X1 and X3 are the ext-bitwise token of --learned-rewrite-rules; this flag now enables X2, X4 and X5 only.

name: pbv-mw-ext-norm
help: umbrella for the extension-normalization rule families of the pbv-mw pass: selects --pbv-mw-trunc-push, --pbv-mw-low-mask, --pbv-mw-ext-bitwise, --pbv-mw-sext-bv1, --pbv-mw-sext-idioms and --learned-rewrite-rules=signed-range as DEFAULTS, so any of them given explicitly wins (e.g. `--pbv-mw-ext-norm --no-pbv-mw-low-mask`). Together they decide, before int-blasting, the instcombine-style multi-width identities over sign/zero extensions and truncations, which the NIA encoding with symbolic powers of two cannot. Disabled by default. NOTE: --learned-rewrite-rules=signed-range no longer exists, and the conditional rules of the other families (T0 T1 T4 T5, X1 X3, S1 S3, I3) moved to --learned-rewrite-rules; this umbrella also adds the ext-norm token of that list (trunc-push,ext-bitwise,sext-bv1,sext-idioms,signed-range) as a default.

name: pbv-mw-low-mask
help: in the pbv-mw pass, turn a conjunction with a zero-extended all-ones value -- the low mask of k ones, `t & (pzero_extend n ones_k)` with ones_k written `(pbvnot (int_to_pbv k 0))` or `(int_to_pbv k -1)` -- into the slice it selects, `(pzero_extend n t[k-1:0])`; a mask with no extension is all ones and the conjunction is t. More generally a conjunction with any zero extension keeps only the low bits of its other operand, `t & (pzero_extend n x) -> (pzero_extend n (t[k-1:0] & x))` for a k-bit x, which puts both sides of a commuted goal in the same shape. Sound with no side condition: the operands have equal widths, so t is (k+n)-bit. The constant-run counterpart of rule M2 of --pbv-mask-slice, which matches only the shifted form `(1 << m) - 1`. Implies the pbv-mw pass is run. Disabled by default.

name: pbv-mw-sext-bv1
help: in the pbv-mw pass, write the sign extension of a 1-bit value c as the negation of its zero extension, `psign_extend n c -> pbvneg (pzero_extend n c)` (sext(1) is all ones, i.e. -1 = -zext(1)), and fold the double negation it exposes, `pbvsub a (pbvneg b) -> pbvadd a b`. Under a bitwise operator the 1-bit sign extension is instead read as the mask it is, a case split on c: `sext(c) & t -> ite(c = 1, t, 0)`, `sext(c) | t -> ite(c = 1, ones, t)`, `sext(c) ^ t -> ite(c = 1, ~t, t)`. The width side condition w(c) = 1 is resolved through the asserted `(= (pbvsize c) 1)` links. This replaces psign_extend's msb ITE and its two pow2 terms by a linear term over a 0/1 value. Implies the pbv-mw pass is run. Disabled by default. NOTE: the conditional rules S1 and S3 are the sext-bv1 token of --learned-rewrite-rules; this flag now enables S2 only.

name: pbv-mw-sext-idioms
help: in the pbv-mw pass, normalize extension idioms: merge nested extensions of the same kind, `EXT n (EXT m x) -> EXT (n+m) x` (pbv-merge-zext/-sext, which the rewriter only runs under --pbv-rw-mw=base|base-cav26); push a sign or zero extension into an ITE, `EXT n (ite c a b) -> ite c (EXT n a) (EXT n b)`; and recognize the shift-pair sign extension, `pbvashr (pbvshl a K) K -> psign_extend n a[w-n-1:0]` for a w-bit a and K = int_to_pbv(w, n) with 0 <= n <= w - 1 entailed. Implies the pbv-mw pass is run. Disabled by default. NOTE: the conditional rule I3 is the sext-idioms token of --learned-rewrite-rules; this flag now enables I1 and I2 only.

name: pbv-mw-shift-bitwise
help: in the pbv-mw pass, move shifts through bitwise operators and normalize bitwise chains: `(a OP b) SH c -> (a SH c) OP (b SH c)` for OP in pbvand/pbvor/pbvxor and SH in pbvshl/pbvlshr/pbvashr (and `~a >>s c -> ~(a >>s c)`), `(x << c) >> c -> x & (ones >> c)` and `(x >> c) << c -> x & (ones << c)`, absorb `ones >> c` next to another `_ >> c` in a conjunction (likewise <<), pull an extension by the same amount out of a bitwise operator (the equal operand widths make the sources equal-width), and flatten/sort/deduplicate and/or/xor chains with their 0/ones operands folded. Every `(pbvsize v)` is first replaced by its width class representative, so the two sides of an identity end up as the same term. All rules are unconditional. Implies the pbv-mw pass is run. Disabled by default. NOTE: the conditional rules W2, W3 and W4 are the shift-bitwise token of --learned-rewrite-rules; this flag now enables W1 and W5 only.

name: pbv-mw-shift-bitwise-w1
help: with --pbv-mw-shift-bitwise, run rule W1, `(a OP b) SH c -> (a SH c) OP (b SH c)`; when off, that flag runs W5 only. W1 is the inverse of M1 of --pbv-mask-slice=all, and with both on preprocessing never terminates; --pbv-rewrites turns both on, so pass --no-pbv-mw-shift-bitwise-w1 with it to avoid the loop. Enabled by default.

name: pbv-mw-sign-idioms
help: in the pbv-mw pass, normalize sign tests: `(x & (1 << (w-1))) = 0 -> ~(x <s 0)`, `-1 <s x` and `0 <=s x -> ~(x <s 0)`, `x <=s -1 -> x <s 0`, the sign broadcast `m >>s (w-1) -> ite(m <s 0, ones, 0)`, a bitwise operator over an ITE with 0/ones branches split into the ITE, an addition pushed into an ITE when that cancels (`(y - z) + z -> y`), and `ite(~c, a, b) -> ite(c, b, a)`. Implies the pbv-mw pass is run. Disabled by default. NOTE: the conditional rules G2a (sgt/sge), G4 and G5c are the sign-idioms token of --learned-rewrite-rules; this flag now enables G1, G2b-d, G3, G5a, G5b and G6 only.

name: pbv-mw-trunc-push
help: in the pbv-mw pass, push a low extract `t[k-1:0]` all the way down: through pbvadd/pbvsub/pbvmul/pbvand/pbvor/pbvxor/pbvnot/pbvneg and ITE (the low k bits of each depend only on the low k bits of its operands), and cut it at an extension `EXT n x` of a w-bit x: to x when w = k, to `x[k-1:0]` when k <= w, and to `EXT (k-w) x` when w <= k, the order being discharged against the asserted width constraints. Unlike rules A/B of --learned-rewrite-rules=preprocess-mw it needs no operand to be an extension of exactly the extract's width, and it revisits the terms it builds, so a chain of pushes reaches the leaves. Implies the pbv-mw pass is run. Disabled by default. NOTE: the conditional rules T0, T1, T4 and T5 are the trunc-push token of --learned-rewrite-rules; this flag now enables T2 and T3 only.

name: pbv-rewrites
help: the T_PBV rewrite rules WITHOUT side conditions of the paper's configuration table (its Table 5) in one flag: --pbv-rw-mw=cav26 (the pbv-c26-* identities), --pbv-rw-ac, --pbv-rw-bool, --pbv-mw-trunc-push (T2, T3), --pbv-mw-low-mask (L), --pbv-mw-ext-bitwise (X2, X4, X5), --pbv-mw-sext-idioms (I1, I2), --pbv-mw-sext-bv1 (S2), --pbv-mw-shift-bitwise (W1 and W5; W1 inverts M1 of --pbv-mask-slice=all and the two can loop, which --no-pbv-mw-shift-bitwise-w1 avoids), --pbv-shift-add-distrib (G), --pbv-mw-sign-idioms (G1-3, G5, G6), --pbv-mask-slice=all (M1), --pbv-uts-mode=flip, and the two unsigned-division identities, --pbv-div-lemmas, the complement rewrite --pbv-rw-and-not, and its dual --pbv-rw-or-not with --pbv-rw-or-not-simple (x | ~y -> ~y + (x & y)). Each is a default only, so any of them given explicitly wins. The rules WITH side conditions are --learned-rewrite-rules=pbv; this flag selects none of them.

name: pbv-rewrites-min
help: exactly the rewrite rules of the paper's RW_B table (Table 6) and nothing else, unlike --pbv-rewrites, which turns on whole families. In the rewriter: xor-ones `x ^ ~0 -> ~x`, not-plus-one `~x + 1 -> -x`, and-not `x & ~y -> x - (x & y)`. In the pbv-mw pass: shift-bitwise `(x sh z) o (y sh z) -> (x o y) sh z` (o in &,|,^; sh in <<,>>,>>a), shl-lshr `x & (~0 >> z) -> (x << z) >> z`, lshr-shl `x & (~0 << z) -> (x >> z) << z`, sext-sext / zext-zext `ext(n, ext(m, x)) -> ext(n+m, x)`, sext-ite / zext-ite `ite(c, ext(n,x), ext(n,y)) -> ext(n, ite(c,x,y))`, sign-bit-and `x & (1 << (k-1)) = 0 -> ~(x <s 0)`, ashr-sign `x >>a (k-1) -> ite(x <s 0, ~0, 0)`, and-lshr-mask `(~0 >> z) & (x >> z) -> x >> z`, and/or/xor/add-ite-mask on `ite(c, 0, ~0)`, sext-zero / zext-zero `ext(n, 0) -> 0`, bitwise-sext / bitwise-zext `ext(n,x) o ext(n,y) -> ext(n, x o y)`. And flip, as --pbv-uts-mode=flip (a default, so an explicit --pbv-uts-mode wins). Five of these run in the opposite direction from rules of other flags (shift-bitwise vs W1 of --pbv-mw-shift-bitwise, shl-lshr / lshr-shl vs W2 of --learned-rewrite-rules=shift-bitwise, sext-ite / zext-ite vs I2 of --pbv-mw-sext-idioms); when the opposite flag is also on, the rule here is skipped, since the two would rewrite back and forth forever. Disabled by default.

name: pbv-rewrites-tuned
help: the subset of --pbv-rewrites that survived a per-family ablation against CVC5-EXP and a leave-one-out inside the subset (sat25 + QF_PBV + fvfp, 60 s): --pbv-rw-bool, --pbv-mw-shift-bitwise (W1, W5), --pbv-rw-and-not, --pbv-uts-mode=flip and --pbv-div-lemmas. Left out: --pbv-rw-mw=cav26 (loses on syrew and alive); --pbv-mask-slice=all (M1 inverts W1 of --pbv-mw-shift-bitwise, and the two loop forever in preprocessing); --pbv-rw-ac, --pbv-mw-ext-bitwise and --pbv-mw-sign-idioms (positive alone, but nothing on top of the five above); and --pbv-mw-trunc-push, --pbv-mw-low-mask, --pbv-mw-sext-idioms, --pbv-mw-sext-bv1, --pbv-shift-add-distrib (no measurable effect). Each is a default only, so any of them given explicitly wins. Its conditional counterpart is the pbv-tuned token of --learned-rewrite-rules.

name: pbv-rw-ac
help: normalize the associative-commutative PBV operators -- the bitwise pbvand, pbvor, pbvxor and the arithmetic pbvadd, pbvmul -- in the rewriter: flatten a nested same-kind chain into its leaf list, order the leaves canonically, drop duplicate leaves for pbvand/pbvor only (idempotence; x xor x is 0, x + x is 2x and x * x is a square, so duplicates must survive there), and rebuild a right-associated binary chain. Two terms that differ only by the associativity or commutativity of these operators then become syntactically identical, so an equality between them closes in the rewriter instead of being handed to the arithmetic solver as a piand query -- which is what the parabit e-graph achieves with its and.assoc/and.commute rules. pbvxor leaves are ordered but NOT deduplicated, since x xor x is 0 rather than x. Note the encoding takes the width of a bitwise term from its FIRST operand, so reordering relies on the admissibility constraints (which equate the operand widths) being asserted, as the translation always does. Disabled by default.

name: pbv-rw-and-not
help: rewrite an and-with-complement into a subtraction: `(pbvand x (pbvnot y))` becomes `(pbvsub x (pbvand x y))`, and symmetrically `(pbvand (pbvnot x) y)` becomes `(pbvsub y (pbvand x y))` (rules pbv-andn-right/pbv-andn-left). Sound because x & y is a bitwise subset of x, so the subtraction never borrows. It removes the pbvnot, so after int-blasting piand(k,x,2^k-1-y) is replaced by x - piand(k,x,y) -- the complement split of --piand-lemmas=complement applied as a rewrite. Binary pbvand only. Disabled by default.

name: pbv-rw-bool
help: decide an equality between two bitwise PBV terms by comparing the Boolean functions they denote. pbvand/pbvor/pbvxor/pbvnot act bitwise and in parallel, so two such terms are equal at EVERY width exactly when their Boolean functions over the shared leaves agree; the rewriter collects the distinct leaves, evaluates both sides over all assignments to them, and rewrites the equality to true when the results match. This decides the whole and/or/xor/not fragment, which the parabit e-graph reaches only by saturating with its bidirectional xor_as_or_and and and_distrib rules -- a destructive rewriter cannot saturate, so it needs a decision procedure instead. A leaf that is not itself bitwise is treated as an independent variable, which is sound (agreement for every value of the leaf implies agreement for its actual value) but means the check can decline a genuine equality rather than assert a false one; `(int_to_pbv k 0)` is recognized as the all-zero constant. Only equality is ever concluded, never disequality: differing tables do not refute the goal, since the leaves need not be independent. Skipped when the term has more than --pbv-rw-bool-cap distinct leaves. Disabled by default.

name: pbv-rw-bool-cap
help: skip the --pbv-rw-bool decision procedure when the two sides together have more than N distinct leaves; the table it builds has 2^N rows.

name: pbv-rw-mw
help: enable the opt-in PBV rewrite rule families (see --pbv-rw-mw=help). These carry no width side condition, so unlike the pbv-mw preprocessing rules they work as ordinary rewrites. The mode selects WHICH family to apply, so that the two can be benchmarked against each other. Disabled by default.

modes.name: none
modes.help: Apply neither family (default).

modes.name: base
modes.help: The `pbv-merge-*` rules plus `pbv-mul-two`: shift-of-shift merge, nested extension merge, and `x * 2 -> x + x`.

modes.name: cav26
modes.help: The `pbv-c26-*` bitwise identities adapted from the parabit (CAV 2026) rule set only.

modes.name: base-cav26
modes.help: Run both families. This is what 'all' used to mean, and what the rw-mw token of --pbv-mw still selects.

modes.name: all
modes.help: The tuned PBV preprocessing line in one flag: the 'cav26' family (NOT 'base'), plus --pbv-uts-mode=flip --pbv-rw-ac --pbv-rw-bool --pbv-shift-add-distrib --pbv-mask-slice=all --pbv-mw-ext-norm --pbv-mw-shift-bitwise --pbv-mw-sign-idioms --pbv-div-lemmas for the unconditional rules, and --learned-rewrite-rules=pbv,int for every conditional family they used to carry (all but shift-guard-elim). Each of those is a default only, so any of them given explicitly on the command line wins.

modes.name: all-no-bug
modes.help: Everything 'all' selects EXCEPT the 'cav26' rewrite family. The generated pbv-c26-* rules (and-one, and-allones, and-self) read only the first two operands of a pbvand without checking its arity, so a 3-ary pbvand loses operands and a valid formula can come back sat (e.g. `(distinct (pbvand t 1 (pbvmul s s)) (pbvand s t 1))` under --decision=stoponly). Every other flag of 'all' is set the same way, as a default only.

name: pbv-rw-nnf
help: push pbvnot inward through pbvand and pbvor (De Morgan), producing a negation normal form: `(pbvnot (pbvand x y))` becomes `(pbvor (pbvnot x) (pbvnot y))` and dually for pbvor. Terminating, since every application moves a negation one level toward the leaves, and together with pbv-not-idemp it drives negations down to the atoms. On its own it enlarges the term; the point is that it is a CANONICAL direction, so two bitwise terms that differ only by De Morgan become syntactically identical and an equality between them closes in the rewriter rather than reaching the arithmetic solver as a piand query. Most effective combined with --pbv-rw-ac (which canonicalizes the and/or nesting) and --pbv-rw-mw=cav26 (which turns `x xor all-ones` into `pbvnot x`, the form these goals are usually written in). This is what the parabit e-graph gets from demorg_and/demorg_or. Disabled by default.

name: pbv-rw-or-not
help: rewrite an or-with-complement into arithmetic: `(pbvor x (pbvnot y))` becomes `(pbvadd (pbvsub ~0 y) (pbvand x y))`, i.e. x | ~y = ~0 - y + (x & y), and symmetrically `(pbvor (pbvnot x) y)` becomes ~0 - x + (x & y) (rules pbv-orn-right/pbv-orn-left); with --pbv-rw-or-not-simple the shorter equivalent form ~y + (x & y) / ~x + (x & y) instead (rules pbv-orns-right/pbv-orns-left). Valid modulo 2^k at every width: x | z = x + z - (x & z) with z = ~y, and x & ~y = x - (x & y); ~y and x & y are bitwise disjoint, so the sum never carries. The dual of --pbv-rw-and-not: after int-blasting the only bitwise term left is piand(k,x,y). Binary pbvor only. Disabled by default; --pbv-rewrites turns it on together with --pbv-rw-or-not-simple, --pbv-rewrites-tuned does not.

name: pbv-rw-or-not-simple
help: with --pbv-rw-or-not, rewrite x | ~y to ~y + (x & y) (and ~x | y to ~x + (x & y)), the form used from 2026-10-20, instead of the original ~0 - y + (x & y). Both are valid at every width; they differ only in the term the int-blaster receives. No effect without --pbv-rw-or-not.

name: pbv-rw-shift-zext-merge
help: merge two shifts separated by a zero extension: `(pbvlshr (pzero_extend n (pbvlshr x y)) z)` becomes `(pbvlshr (pzero_extend n x) (pbvadd (pzero_extend n y) z))`, and dually for pbvshl. The existing pbv-merge-lshr/shl rules require the two shifts to be adjacent, so they never match a MULTI-WIDTH goal, where the intermediate width appears as exactly such an extension between them -- and by the time the term reaches the mod-reduction pass the int-blaster has already purified the divisions into skolems, so the integer-level nested-division merge cannot see them either. Zero extension preserves the value, so the composition is x div 2^(y+z), the same identity pbv-merge-lshr proves for adjacent shifts, and it carries the same overflow guard on y+z. Disabled by default.

name: pbv-shift-add-distrib
help: in the pbv-mw pass, pull a left shift out from under a matching right shift: `((x << c) + y) >> c` becomes `x + (y >> c)`, looking through the zero extensions that a multi-width goal puts on every operand and requiring the two shift amounts to agree once those are stripped. This is parabit's div_mult_self, `(x + y*z) div y = (x div y) + z`, in the only place cvc5 can still apply it: the int-blaster purifies its divisions into skolems while translating, so no integer-level rule can see the pattern afterwards. The rewrite is valid only when `x << c` does not overflow the width it is computed at, which for a p-bit x and a u-bit shift amount is `s >= p + (2^u - 1)` -- a NON-linear condition, discharged against the order facts, where 2^u is treated as an opaque atom so the constraint is linear in {s, p, 2^u} and matches the precondition such goals state verbatim. Disabled by default. NOTE: rule F itself, the shl pull-out described above, is conditional and is no longer selected here -- it is the shift-add-distrib token of --learned-rewrite-rules. This flag now enables only rule G, `zext(n, x >> y) -> zext(n,x) >> zext(n,y)`.

The checker makes that distinction visible: whether an unsat answer comes from the formula not being well-sorted, or from the bit-vector constraints themselves. The mode chooses WHAT checker to run (shallow or deep) and WHEN to run it (before or after solving).

name: piand-lemmas
help: comma-separated list of extra lemma schemas for the parametric integer-and (PIAND) nl-ext solver; combine freely, e.g. 'complement,low-c-bits'. Tokens: none (default); carry (full-refine carry upper bound: 2*piand(k,x,y) <= x+y under x,y in [0,2^k)); lsb (full-refine LSB equivalence: piand(k,x,y) mod 2 = (x mod 2)*(y mod 2) under k>0); width-monotone (pairwise full-refine width narrowing: x,y in [0,2^k1) /\ k1<=k2 => piand(k1,x,y) = piand(k2,x,y)); complement (init-refine complement split: x,y in [0,2^k) => piand(k,x,y) + piand(k,x,2^k-1-y) = x; every bit of x meets a set bit in exactly one of y and ~y, which is what a subset hypothesis such as `(~a | b) = ones` -- the must-be-consistent-bits predicate of the icfb benchmarks -- reduces to; it introduces piand(k,x,2^k-1-y), whose own complement folds back, and introduced terms are never expanded again); complement-existing (the same split, but only between two PIAND terms that are BOTH already present, matched up to rewriting and argument order and re-checked at every last call; never introduces a term); complement-both (complement,complement-existing; pairs already covered by an introduced split are not emitted twice); complement-sym (also split on x: piand(k,x,y) + piand(k,2^k-1-x,y) = y, introducing piand(k,2^k-1-x,y)); mask (init-refine constant low-mask evaluation: piand(k,2^j-1,y) = y mod 2^min(j,k) for y in [0,2^k), split into k>=j and 1<=k<j so the common case has the constant modulus 2^j; covers the bit-0 extraction piand(k,1,y) of `pbvand x 1` / `pbvor x 1` that the rewriter cannot fold at symbolic k); lean (the lean iand-style full-refine bounds, same as --piand-lean-refine); low-c-bits (init-refine low-bit upper bounds, for every c = 1..N with N = --piand-low-c-bits: piand(k,x,y) mod 2^c <= x mod 2^c and <= y mod 2^c; unconditional, and every modulus is a constant, so no PIAND or EXP term is introduced); align (init-refine aligned operand: j>=0 /\ 0<=x<2^j => piand(k,x,y) = 0 for every power 2^j that y is syntactically a multiple of, e.g. y = (z*2^j) mod 2^k, a left shift by j -- the low j bits of y are zero and x has bits only there, and for j>k y masks to 0; when y is a multiple of 2^k itself, piand(k,x,y) = 0 outright. Alignment is found through sums, products, ITE, mod 2^k, PIAND at the same width and purification skolems. It decides `t & (z << t)`-style terms, where t < 2^t, which no other schema here does); align-id (init-refine aligned identity: k>0 /\ j>=0 /\ 0<=x<2^j /\ x<2^k => piand(k,x,y) = x for y = (x + m) mod 2^k with m a multiple of 2^j, e.g. `s & (s + (t << s))`). Neither align schema introduces a PIAND or EXP term. mask-sym (full-refine symbolic low mask: 0<=j<=k => piand(k,x,2^j-1) = x mod 2^j for an argument congruent to 2^j-1 mod 2^k with 2^j an existing power term, e.g. `(1 << t) - 1`); overlap-lb (full-refine lower bound: x,y in [0,2^k) => piand(k,x,y) >= x+y-2^k+1, since x|y <= 2^k-1); subset-trans (existing terms only: piand(k,a,b)=a /\ piand(k,b,c)=b => piand(k,a,c)=a); subset-mono (existing terms only: piand(k,x,x')=x => piand(k,x,y) <= piand(k,x',y)); pow2-idiom (existing terms only: 0<c<2^k /\ piand(k,c,c-1)=0 => piand(k,y,c-1) = y mod c; the c<2^k guard is required, piand(2,6,5)=0 but piand(2,3,5)=1). The three existing-term schemas match arguments up to their residue mod 2^k; they never introduce a term. All five are full-refine schemas: a lemma is sent only when the current model falsifies it. Aggregate: all (carry,lsb,width-monotone,complement,mask,lean). An unknown token is an error.

modes.name: pbv
modes.help: Lift BV input to PBV and translate it with the PBV int-blaster (PIntBlaster) INSIDE the bv-to-int pass, i.e. before the `rewrite`, `pbv-mw` and `pbv-to-int` passes run. Those passes therefore never see the lifted terms: the PBV rewriter families (--pbv-rw-ac, --pbv-rw-bool, --pbv-rw-mw), the multi-width pass (--learned-rewrite-rules=preprocess-mw, --learned-rewrite-rules=sext-to-zext, --pbv-shift-add-distrib, --pbv-mask-slice) and the pbv-to-int post-passes (--learned-rewrite-rules=int, --pbv-type-check) are selected but have nothing to act on. Use `pbv-pipeline` to get them. This mode also selects the tuned PBV configuration as DEFAULTS: --arith-exp-lemmas=exp-full --analyze-exp-instances=multiply-only-relate --learned-rewrite-rules=preprocess-mw --pbv-rw-ac --learned-rewrite-rules=sext-to-zext --pbv-rw-bool --pbv-shift-add-distrib --pbv-rw-mw=cav26 --pbv-mask-slice=all --learned-rewrite-rules=int --piand-lemmas=complement --decision=stoponly --pbv-uts-mode=flip --pbv-lift-uf. Each is a default only, so any of them given explicitly on the command line wins, e.g. `--solve-bv-as-int=pbv --pbv-rw-mw=none` subtracts one family; an explicit --pbv-mw=LIST likewise overrides the families it names.

modes.name: pbv-pipeline
modes.help: Lift BV input to PBV in the bv-to-int pass and STOP there, leaving the lifted PBV assertions (plus one `(= (pbvsize pbv_x) k)` width pin per lifted variable) in the pipeline, so that they then go through exactly the passes a native PBV input does: `rewrite` (the PBV rewriter, --pbv-rw-*), `pbv-mw` and `pbv-to-int` (the PBV int-blaster with its --pbv-uts-mode, --learned-rewrite-rules=int and --pbv-type-check post-passes), followed by the exp passes. This is the mode in which every PBV improvement applies to a bit-vector input; `pbv` translates before those passes run. Model values for the original BV variables are recovered by pbv-to-int as `((_ nat2bv k) chi(pbv_x))`. Selects the same tuned defaults as `pbv`, including --pbv-lift-uf. An assertion containing a BV operator the lifter does not handle (bvcomp, the overflow predicates) makes the whole run fall back to native bit-vectors, as in `pbv`.

modes.name: pbv-direct
modes.help: Translate BV input with the PBV int-blaster (PIntBlaster) DIRECTLY, with no BV-to-PBV lifting at all: no pbv_x variables, no `(= (pbvsize pbv_x) k)` pins and no kappa skolems. Each fixed-width BV term is handled as the PBV term of the same shape whose width is the literal width of its sort, so every `(** 2 k)` the translation writes has a constant exponent and folds. The translation and its options (--pbv-uts-mode other than flip, --pbv-to-int-use-pow2, ...) are the PBV ones, and the arithmetic side of the tuned PBV configuration (--arith-exp-lemmas=exp-full, --piand-lemmas=complement, --decision=stoponly, ...) is selected as defaults exactly as for `pbv`. The PBV-level rewrites (--pbv-rw-*, the pbv-mw pass, --pbv-uts-mode=flip) do not apply, since there are no PBV terms for them to act on; use `pbv-pipeline` for those. Falls back to native bit-vectors, as `pbv` does, when an assertion holds a BV operator the blaster has no case for (rotate, repeat, bvcomp, the overflow predicates) or a quantifier over a bit-vector sort. Models for the BV variables are recovered as `((_ int_to_bv k) chi(x))`.
